429625b-rmtree.description:
fix(orchestrator): a plan folder is deleted only directly under plans.dir (#281)

* fix(orchestrator): a plan folder is deleted only directly under plans.dir

plan check, plan approve and plan amend refuse a discarding folder plan whose resolved parent is not the
resolved plans.dir; the driver refuses to start on one, and checks again at the deletion itself, for a discard
and for a promote's archive tree, so a config that moved mid-run deletes nothing and the Lead is told the folder
and plans.dir. A discard plan's archive still runs the gaps reviewer.

* style(orchestrator): ruff format the plans.dir guard tests

* test(orchestrator): the plans.dir run test passes the typed route file

fix(orchestrator): a FAIL under an earlier approval digest no longer makes a PASS flaky (#274)

The D16 flaky rule matched prior receipts by tree only. After plan amend, an oracle's new
bytes passing on a tree where the old bytes failed was marked UNKNOWN (flaky). Match the
digest too, in a pure is_flaky helper with unit tests.

e9bd1ad-checks.description:
fix(orchestrator): require each worker check once and keep a required command out of the forbidden line (#316)

Tiers that render the same check listed it twice, so the worker was asked to
run one command twice; and a `full` equal to a required check was handed to
the worker as the command not to run, forbidding a check it must pass.
Equivalent commands (a launcher prefix apart) now fold into one requirement,
a distinct `full` stays the verify/CI-owned line, and COMPLETE validation is
decided by the same set: the `affected` not_run allowance no longer waives a
command another tier also requires.

stale-team/t1r1.description:
fix(runtime): the live-lead refusal advises only what can be followed

LEAD_ID cannot carry a real generation: a pid:lstart stamp has spaces, so
"pass --lead <generation>" told the caller to do something impossible.
The refusal now offers that way out only when the generation can be
passed, and otherwise names the terminal's own hc terminal as the way out.

review-gate/t2r2.description:
docs(orchestrator): read a null requirement violation as absent

A review item may carry `requirement_violation` as an optional field, so a
producer that serialises it always writes `null` when nothing is asserted. The
readers already treated that as absent, but R136 said any non-object metadata
is refused, which promised a refusal nobody implemented and nothing tested.

The requirement now says a present metadata value that is neither an object nor
`null` is refused, and names the null behaviour: it asserts nothing, so both
readers read it as absent and the reviewer is not sent to repair a shape that
claims nothing. The S3 metadata test covers the null case on a concern and on a
blocking item, through both readers, so the row's coverage proves the sentence.

pr408.description:
fix(agent-review): start the reviewer the way its own CLI runs, and keep the screening it stopped after

A deep review now asks its harness one question in that harness's own
non-interactive mode, with the prompt on stdin: `claude -p` and `pi -p` both
read the prompt there and print the answer, so no variadic option of theirs can
read the prompt as another tool name. The arguments that hold a family to
reading and searching and the flag that makes it answer at all come from one
table in agent-runtime, so a family cannot answer with controls and then be
started without the mode that runs it.

A reviewer that cannot start, times out or exits nonzero is an incomplete
execution, not a refusal: the provider already answered, so report.json is
written with the screening's judgments, its usage and the escalation that asked
for the review, and the stop is named in `failure.reason` and in the review's
own record, with the exit code saying incomplete. The run is never retried and
never falls back to another model.

The runtime answers `cannot(family)` beside `run(family)`, and a stub harness on
PATH proves every family the runtime holds receives the prompt whole and its
controls, while each family it cannot hold is refused by name with the reason
its own sandbox falls short. A family added to the runtime's list fails a test
until it is answered one way or the other.

pr409.description:
fix(structure): measure the files the branch carries, not only the committed ones

Asking git for `--cached` alone left a file the branch adds but has not committed
unmeasured, so a new module over a ceiling passed the gate that S3 and S8 promise.
The budget's listing now asks for tracked and untracked-but-not-ignored files, the
same question the plan check asks, and drops the cache trees by hand because
`--others` lifts `.venv/`, `node_modules/` and `__pycache__/` back in. A nested
checkout and an ignored directory are still unlisted: git reports the first as one
directory entry and never sees the second.

The plan side keeps `--others` — a module pytest imports is one whether or not it
was committed, and R40's refusal test writes an untracked one — so its S23 node now
builds both copies git does not read as modules: one in an ignored tree, one in a
nested checkout. A plain untracked copy under the package is still refused; that is
the tension between S23's wording and R40, and it is the plan owner's to narrow.
